### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **9** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **142** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/index.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**56** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/index.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 41 pages)`
- **24** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **156** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eff052401cfbee71865fe9a2868f6f579fbd8f61` — the merge of head `d28f4cff56ee14c06afa52c7753e2f30537ccff9` into base `92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eff052401cfbee71865fe9a2868f6f579fbd8f61 && git checkout eff052401cfbee71865fe9a2868f6f579fbd8f61
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175 d28f4cff56ee14c06afa52c7753e2f30537ccff9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175 && git merge --no-ff d28f4cff56ee14c06afa52c7753e2f30537ccff9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `02321084fc90276ef297814e454b9ba669e7afe6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/migration.zod.ts + packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-not-null.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts, packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts, packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts, packages/runtime/src/index.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/declared-webhooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-provenance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/index.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-secret.object.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-flow-credential.object.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/organization-ownership-boot-refusal-order.dogfood.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.generation-1.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-not-null.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.kernel.test.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-drift.test.ts, content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json, .changeset/24581-organization-ownership-ceremony-open.md; read beside the diff for the judgments below: packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/sys-webhook.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/declared-webhooks.test.ts

Read: cards #24581 and #24582; claims 6276776808 and 6276790571; seat note 6271949316; rulings 6266750393, 6267391172, 6269955919 with its amendment 6270010349, and 6270035914 on #15194; ruling 6278609968 on #24580; step 0's plan 6268559156 (steps[4], steps[5], F1 to F6); the dev's report 6279428591; the Landed records 6279236728 (#24529), 6275112954 (#24530), 6272692402 (#24531); #24489; #24625 (measured record 6278938192, claim 6278944518); the head's check-runs twice. Diff: 66 files, +2,797 / -737, head `02321084` verified; merge-base with `origin/main` `7c509c286`; `origin/main` at `eadea5720`.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. 5a, webhooks (`organization-ownership-apply.ts`, `runDeclaredWebhooks` 3178-3330).** Holds.
- Selection is by shape: `managed_by IN ('package','platform')` (`SEEDED_PROVENANCE` 2985, used at 3187), then only names a package still declares (3199-3200). Never by NULL.
- Pristine mirrors: deliveries re-sourced first to `declared:NAME` (3258, `DECLARED_WEBHOOK_REF_PREFIX` 2992) with a count-back that throws if any still name the row (3226-3240), then the copy is deleted by id with the seeded predicate re-asserted and read back (3241-3247, 3259). Pinned: generation-1 test 312-325 asserts the UPDATE precedes the DELETE, and 351-353 pins the spelling equal to plugin-webhooks' `declaredWebhookRefId` (now exported, `plugin-webhooks/src/index.ts`).
- Customized mirrors: a switch-only edit (`isSwitchOnlyEdit` 3129-3142: every column the 18.0 seeder mapped, label / object_name / triggers / url / method / description, still equals the `definition_json` snapshot, and no credential is stored, 3132) becomes the declaration's `sys_metadata_activation` row with that switch (3257, `setActivation` 3014-3064 reads back), deliveries re-sourced, copy deleted. Any other edit is renamed in place to a free `NAME_custom` (3264-3279, `freeName` 3070-3082 within `NAME_MAX`), `managed_by 'admin'`, `customized false`, snapshot stripped of provenance (3265, 3270), and the declaration is switched off (3280). The clone keeps its id, so its deliveries' tail already names the clone's row id, which is what seat note 6271949316 asked for. A credential-bearing row is always a clone (3132; test 355-360). Pinned 327-349.
- Orphaned ciphers: the `sys_secret` ids a deleted copy referenced are deleted once no webhook row references them (3288-3305); test 312-325 (`secretsDeleted: 1`, `sec_setting` kept).
- Mirror predicate aligned: `classifyDeclaredNameHolder` now uses `isSeededProvenance` (`declared-webhooks.ts` diff), the same pair the provenance hook stamps (`webhook-provenance.ts` diff) and the ceremony reads. Inventory `sys_webhook` category `where managed_by in [package, platform]` (`organization-ownership-inventory.ts` diff), kept a category not a departure so an undeclared seeded row (a live webhook) is still attributed; such rows stay and are reported (3201-3208; test 343-348).
- Post-condition verified: no seeded row holds a declared name after the step (3307-3317). Blocks, writing nothing, when the run has no registry to read (3192-3198; test 387-391).

**2. 5b, sibling moves (`runSiblingMoves` 3456-3521, `SIBLING_MOVES` 3353-3379).** Holds; F3 holds.
- Global audit rows: `scope = 'global'` (3358), to `sys_platform_setting_audit`. Identity mail: `related_object = 'sys_user'` plus the magic-link clause (3369-3377). Neither reads `organization_id`; the copy excludes `ORG` (3478); the delete re-asserts the selector by id (3511); read-back before delete (3506-3509); already-moved rows are not copied twice (3483-3488; test 304-310). Inventory gains the two departures `identity-mail-move` and `global-audit-move` (`organization-ownership-inventory.ts` diff), both `as: 'moved'`.
- Mail jobs first: `rewriteMailJobs` (3393-3425) runs before the chunks (3479), over `email.send.async` and `email.attachment.reclaim` pending or running jobs whose `{rowId}` is a moving row and whose `object` is absent or `sys_email` (3413); payload and metadata gain `object: 'sys_identity_email'`, and the idempotency key takes the sibling spelling for both the row and the `_attachments` key (3417-3419). Test 276-293.
- `sys_activity` rows re-pointed on every rotation shard by `(object_name, record_id)` after each chunk (3510, 3524-3540); the audit ledger is left alone by design. Test 295-302. Seat note said re-point or delete; re-point is done. `sys_activity` carries only `object_name` / `record_id` as its record linkage (`plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-activity.object.ts` 163, 198), so nothing is left pointing at the old object.
- Exposure (#24625): nothing on `sys_email` is widened; the moved rows land behind `requiredPermissions` on `sys_identity_email`.

**DECISION 2, the magic-link selector (apply.ts 3344-3351, 3369-3377): `related_object IS NULL AND related_id IS NULL AND (body_text LIKE '%/magic-link/verify?token=%' OR body_html LIKE ...)`.** Reliability: the link is the mail's purpose, so every rendering of `auth.magic_link` carries it, and better-auth's verify path is fixed for the 18.0 line; the pattern is bound as a parameter (no placeholder confusion, no `_` wildcard in it). What it can misclassify, and in which direction: (a) a false positive, a non-identity mail with no related record whose body quotes a sign-in link (an app or notification mail that pasted one) is moved INTO `sys_identity_email`, the stricter table (`manage_platform_settings`), and loses its organization stamp, which under `single` is the Default Organization; that errs safe for exposure and loses nothing a reader needs. The dev's own out-of-scope finding is the same direction: an app mail sent with a caller-supplied `relatedObject 'sys_user'` moves too. (b) A false negative, a magic-link row whose body carries no such path (a customized template that omitted the URL text, or a row with `related_id` set) stays in `sys_email`; under `single` it is stamped (F3), so the NOT NULL step is not held back, and its body is covered by the #24625 column-wide gate; under a wall an organization-less miss is unattributable and blocks attribution, which fails closed (see ③3 for the misdirecting remedy). No misclassification moves a row to a LESS gated table. Ablated red (3). **Accept.**

**3. 5c, 9c (`runDeclaredRuleCopies` 3570-3676).** Holds. A copy is any row that is not a pristine mirror (`copyWhere` 3582-3589, so customized seeded copies and admin rows a declaration collided with), under a name the registry declares (3605-3622). Each is renamed in place to a free `NAME_custom`, `managed_by 'admin'`, `customized false` (3645-3657), its id and so its `sys_record_share.source_id` grants kept; the declaration's `sharing_rule` activation row is written `active: false` (3662), and grants naming the declaration itself are removed and counted (3663-3672). Pristine mirrors stay the mirror-deletion step's. Blocks, writing nothing, without a registry while a customized copy exists (3590-3604; `declared-rule-mirrors.test.ts` diff pins that the step blocks first and `mirror-deletion` is not reached). Test 362-374 and the idempotence case 426-432.

**DECISION 1, the walled block (apply.ts 3209-3219 for webhooks, 3624-3633 for rules; test 376-385).** Under `group` or `isolated`, a customized copy of a declared item blocks its step before any write, naming each row by id and name and the remedy. Consistency with ruling A (6278609968): the switch is one `sys_metadata_activation` row, deployment-level and operator-gated under a wall; switching it off for one organization's customization would remove the declared webhook or rule from every organization, which is exactly the silent cross-organization loss #24435 rejected. Under `single` the ceremony does decide (one organization, one switch), and the end state equals what 18.0 served: the customized row answered and the declaration was withheld; now the clone answers and the declaration is off, so no access changes silently there, and the grants 5c removes are named in the report (`grantsRemoved`). Pristine copies under a wall are deleted only when no customized copy exists (3209-3219 returns before any write); the PR body's "pristine copies are still deleted under a wall" is true in that case only. Actionable remedy: rename to an undeclared name (step 4's 409 guard refuses only a rename ONTO a declared name, `bindDeclaredWebhookNameGuard` on #24667; `bindDeclaredRuleNameGuard` likewise), or delete; then set the switch through the activation door, which under a wall is the operator's, and the operator is who runs the ceremony; then re-run. Each step names its rows. **Accept.** The remedy would be stronger if the reviewed plan named the copies before `--apply` (③4).

**4. 5d, NOT NULL after the moves (`runNotNull` 3724-3760; `organization-ownership-not-null.ts`).** Holds under ② A. Candidates are the post-move plan's `attribution` / `report` tables with a present column, `notNull.willReceive` and `organizationNull === 0` (3731-3736); every physical table, siblings routed by `database` (3735, command 866-888). The door is the driver's own drift apply with a ceremony-authored `tighten_not_null` entry (`not-null.ts` 60-73): `not-declared` for an undeclared table (36-39), `unsupported` for a rotation shard (40-49) and for a transport with `driftApplyLimit` (55-59, the Turso remote face), `failed` blocks (apply.ts 3754-3756). The differ exemption is exactly one condition, `relax_not_null` on `fieldName === ceremonyOwnedNullability` (`schema-drift.ts` diff at the one `expectNullable && !col.nullable && field.required !== true` branch), fed by `SqlDriver.resolveTenantField(tableName)` (`sql-driver.ts` diff): a NOT NULL on any other column is still reported (pin: `sql-driver-schema-drift.test.ts`, `note` still yields `relax_not_null`), type, missing-column, unmapped-column and index drift on the tenant column are untouched, and a table whose tenant field is not `organization_id` or is absent gets no exemption. No metadata changed. `not-null.test.ts` 54 drives the real door and re-scans. Masks no other drift.

**5. Step 6.**
- #24489 items 1, 4, 6: `MigrateOrganizationOwnership` and `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_UPGRADE_UNAVAILABLE*` deleted, `export default class OrganizationOwnershipCeremony` (`organization-ownership.ts` 320); `organization-ownership.release-refusal.test.ts` deleted; dogfood boot-refusal-order step 2 runs the real binary and 2a is dropped (diff); the 16 test files import the default. `DeclaredWebhooksPort` (registry first, metadata service second, each item parsed by `WebhookSchema`, 835-860) and `NotNullPort` (862-888) wired in the command. `os dev` names the ceremony again (`dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts` diff) and the drop gate's human face names its two steps (`apply.ts` diff); both pinned with `not.toMatch(/17\.x/)`.
- Birth marker and guard: `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_SHAPE_GENERATION = 1`, `OrganizationOwnershipBirthMarkerSchema` `{shapeGeneration, platformVersion, commit optional, createdAt}`, `organizationOwnershipShapeGenerationOf` reading birth then checkpoint, else 0 (`migration.zod.ts` diff). The guard decides on generation alone: verified at or above current boots (`boot-guard.ts` 542-550); absent plus no v17 table plus the ledger's own store created from empty writes the marker once (551-570, `writeBirthMarker` 488-514, `commit` absent because no build records it, 491); otherwise refused, a verified lower generation as `outdated` naming both generations (571-578, 284-291) which is F5; unverified and unreadable refused as before (306-312, 299-304). The ceremony's checkpoint carries `shapeGeneration` (apply.ts 374-391, 3957-3960, 4165). The telemetry-sibling case of ruling ①A item 1 is handled by judging the ledger store's own stats (474-482). Every CLI boot writes the birth half: `OrganizationOwnershipBirthMarkerPlugin` (373-406, never refuses) in `createStandaloneStack` (`standalone-stack.ts` diff). Pins: boot-guard.test.ts 162 (R1), 177 (18.0 database refused), 199 (F5), 294 (the birth half), kernel test 174 and 192. But see B1 for the one served transport whose store can never read as created from empty.
- Flips: `systemFields: { tenant: false }` on `sys_secret` and `sys_flow_credential` (object diffs), inventory fates to `column-drop`, settings writer no longer stamps the cipher and `SettingsSecretStore.insert` no longer takes `organization_id` (service-settings diffs; `settings-secret-organization.test.ts` restated). Harness case 3 asserts both columns gone (270).
- Refusal text (271-313) names no release line; one sentence covers v17 and 18.0 databases, plus the `outdated` arm. Harness 159 pins no `17.x`.
- `tenancy: { enabled: false }` and `systemFields: false` read by the v17 probe (`declaresNoOrganizationColumn` 224-231; test 138).
- `migration.zod.ts` prohibition amended for this marker only, stated as "claims no ceremony ran: it records that none was owed", consistent with ①A.

**6. The 18.x line rule after this lands.** The harness (`upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts`) names R2 and R3: `1. R2, restated` (155, refused, no marker written), `1b. R2, restated` (168, the real binary plans and applies in the showcase's directory, `expectCertified` 106-118 reads `checkpoint.shapeGeneration` equal to the current generation), `1c. R2, restated` (176, boots), `2` and `2b` (186, 202: one delivery `declared:NAME`), `3` (231: moved, re-sourced, deleted, columns dropped, NOT NULL on five tenant tables), `4. R3, restated` (281: v17 trait refused, ceremony, boots). R1 is pinned by name in the guard's unit test (162) and kernel test (174), not in the harness; the cards asked the harness for R2 and R3 by name, which it holds. R4 is step 4's, in #24667's restored e2e cases. 8/8 reported green after the main merge.

**7. Ablations and gates.** Eleven legs, each red then restored to `blob == HEAD`, including the generation rule (F5), birth only on a store created from empty, the `tenancy.enabled` spelling, both 5b selectors, the mail-job rewrite, the delivery re-source, the switch-only reading, the rule switch-off, the NULL hold-back and the differ exemption; every leg maps to a claim above. Gates: 137 derived, 131 exit 0 on the first sweep, 6 fixed (two census regenerations, the engine-double predicate, the spec parsed alias, the CLI test alias, with `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` NOT MEASURED on the shallow clone), 132 re-derived after the merge all green; `check-governed-merges --branch`: 0 of 95 governed paths, 3,534 changed lines so Tier H. Head check-runs at the second read: Lint and Repo Gates, every Lint lane, Type Check source gates and debt ledger, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the claim guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate all `success`; Test Core 1 to 6, Type Check workspace and Type Check consumer gates still `in_progress`; the opt-in lanes `skipped`. The verdict below does not wait on them; the seat reads them before queueing.

**8. Complete feature.** The command runs, the harness upgrades an 18.0 and a v17 database through the real binary and boots them, `os dev` upgrades in place, the docs and checklist (`cli.json` revision 3) say the ceremony is open. Nothing dormant on this head.

**9. Interactions.**
- `serve.ts`: this PR's diff on it is empty; #24667 (head `fdfc84238`) deletes the `walledPostureRefusal` call and function and the `postureEnforcesWall` import. Nothing on `serve.ts` to reconcile. The two PRs do meet on `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` and `plugin-webhooks/src/declared-webhooks.ts`: a trial `merge-tree` of the two heads auto-merges `declared-webhooks.ts` (this PR edits `classifyDeclaredNameHolder` and adds `isSeededProvenance`; #24667 appends the 409 guard; independent) and CONFLICTS on `cli.mdx`, where #24667 keeps "Until then the ceremony refuses … Keep a v17 database on a 17.x release" (its 204-209, 1202, 1482-1486) and this PR removes those sentences. Whichever lands second (this one) must keep this PR's paragraphs and carry #24667's "every tenancy posture" clause (B2).
- #24661 (`a78914818` on main) is not an ancestor of this head: the seven `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/` entries saying "18.0 supports fresh installs only and does not upgrade a v17 database: keep a v17 database on a 17.x release" arrive with the required main merge and are false once this lands (B2).
- #24625 read gate (`claude/issue-24625-identity-mail-read-gate`, head `e7f2dd039`): no path overlap with this PR. That branch is selector-free by design: it gates `body_text` / `body_html` on both tables and the mirrors for every row, stating that no column tells an 18.0 identity row apart. So there is no second identity selector to share; the ceremony's (apply.ts 3353-3379) is the only one, and the two are consistent: after the move the gate still covers tenant mail on `sys_email`, and a selector miss (DECISION 2b) stays behind the gate.

**10. Semver and the Clause-② arm.** See ②.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on eight packages, marked `!`, under the launch-window convention for breaking changes (ADR-0131 D10; `check-changeset-no-major` holds the ceiling; Check Changeset `success`). Consistent with the content: breaking for every database an earlier release created (refused at boot until the ceremony; `os migrate organization-ownership` exits 0 where 18.0 exited 1 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, and the cli exports `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_UPGRADE_UNAVAILABLE` / `_CODE` are deleted); two objects lose their organization column; `SettingsSecretStore.insert` loses an optional property (narrowing); new additive spec exports `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_SHAPE_GENERATION`, `OrganizationOwnershipBirthMarkerSchema`, `organizationOwnershipShapeGenerationOf`, runtime `OrganizationOwnershipBirthMarkerPlugin`, plugin-webhooks `DECLARED_WEBHOOK_REF_PREFIX` / `declaredWebhookRefId` / `isSeededProvenance`. ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right: no metadata key moves; the data migration is the operator's ceremony, named by the refusal. Clause-② arm: the PR body and changeset read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; `reviewFace` on the changed paths decides the schema face (`migration.zod.ts`), so the tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` whatever that line says; the mixed spelling is noted, not held against the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Merge instructions for the landing** (B2): resolve the `cli.mdx` conflict with #24667 in this PR's favour plus step 4's "every tenancy posture" clause; restate #24661's seven semantic entries to the ceremony prescription; re-run the harness on the merged tree; re-review at the new head.
2. **Plan versus apply on the identity selector.** The inventory departure `identity-mail-move.where` is `related_object = 'sys_user'` alone (`organization-ownership-inventory.ts` diff); the apply adds the magic-link clause (apply.ts 3369-3377). Under `single` every row is stamped (F3) so the departure counts nothing and the difference is invisible.
